newsitem.title: UK: Euro bourses mixed, London claws back loss.
newsitem.headline: Euro bourses mixed, London claws back loss.

text.p: European bourses were mixed on Tuesday with London clawing back most of its early losses as investors regained confidence after being spooked by a poor performance in New York overnight.
Wall Street's negative close on Monday also unsettled the dollar, already hit by uncertainty over Tokyo's monetary direction ahead of the important Japanese Tankan economic survey out on Wednesday.
Stocks in London started the week badly after a three-day weekend, slipping 0.3 percent, but bargain-hunters later moved in and the FTSE index recovered most of the lost ground.

Tuesday's patchy showing in London followed a string of records last week, culminating in Friday's trading high of 3,911, fuelled by a wave of European interest rate cuts. But a lack of scheduled economic and company news was likely to cap activity in a traditionally slack holiday period.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average slipped nearly 29 points to 5,694 on Monday in one of the slowest trading days of 1996 as U.S. Treasuries were again pressured by inflationary fears.
The worries were sparked by minutes of the policy-making Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meeting last month, which showed a bias among the members towards tightening interest rates.
In Frankfurt, German shares were unsettled by Wall Street's close but slowly climbed into positive territory after losses early in the session.

By mid-morning, stocks traded on the floor and on the computerised IBIS DAX index were both up a few points. Dealers hoped volumes would pick up after reaching a year's low on Monday because of London's closure.
French shares were weaker for the second day running amid growing unease about a difficult autumn for the government which also weighed on the franc, dealers said.

Bond prices were weaker and the franc was quoted at 3.4210 per mark for the first time since August 13 as worries about the government's autumn budget and a weak U.S. currency lifted the mark and squeezed French investments.
The dollar, which dropped sharply on Monday because of jitters over the Japanese Tankan survey, weakened further against the mark to 1.4749.

"There is a slight bias for a weaker dollar but it's still within its recent 1.4700-1.4950 mark range," said a Swiss bank dealer. "The main focus this week is the Tankan but nobody is really anticipating any change in Japan rates."

Foreign exchange markets regard the Tankan report as an important pointer to the country's monetary policy stance. If it points to weakness in the economy, the report will help the dollar regain some lost ground as speculation of a near-term rise in Japanese interest rates will evaporate.
The Japanese discount rate is currently at a record low of 0.5 percent.
The dollar was also pressured by the mark's strength against European currencies amid renewed concerns over Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) timetable.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was at 1.4749 marks and 107.75 yen compared with 1.4789 marks and 107.55 yen at the London close on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
The London stock market was down 0.8 points to 3906.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 4.12 points to 2,016.30.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt was up 6.72 points at 2,559.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $389.00 an ounce, compared with Monday's close of $388.75 on international markets. Silver was up five cents at $5.28.
